# arecipe

> A free family recipe box and sharing app built on the AT Protocol. There is
> no backend: every recipe is a public record owned by its author, and arecipe
> is one client among many that reads and writes them.

For AI agents: read the agent guide before extracting anything. It explains
how to read arecipe's data as public AT Protocol records instead of scraping
HTML, reports what the primary United States sources say about recipes and
copyright (quoted and linked — arecipe adds no legal conclusions of its own),
and describes the extraction practices this project follows itself.

## Docs

- [Agent guide (canonical)](https://arecipe.app/agents.md): how to extract, normalize, attribute, and share recipes properly, and how to read arecipe's public records the way the protocol intends.
- [Agent guide (HTML mirror)](https://arecipe.app/agents.html): the same guide, generated from the canonical Markdown for human readers.
- [Lexicon and NSID registry](https://github.com/CroftCommunity/arecipe/blob/main/docs/LEXICONS.md): every AT Protocol record type arecipe creates or consumes, with field-level notes.

## Data access

- [Read the records, not the pages](https://arecipe.app/agents.html#part-c-read-the-records-not-the-pages): recipes are exchange.recipe.recipe records in each author's PDS repository; resolve handle to DID to PDS, then use com.atproto.repo.listRecords and getRecord. No key, no scraping.

## Reading order

- [What the sources say](https://arecipe.app/agents.html#part-a-what-the-sources-say): the primary U.S. sources on recipes and copyright, quoted and linked.
- [Best practices for extraction](https://arecipe.app/agents.html#part-b-best-practices-for-extracting-recipes): prefer structured data, take the facts, re-express instructions, attribute, be a polite client.
- [Plain notice](https://arecipe.app/agents.html#part-d-plain-notice): informational only; all cited sources are U.S. sources.
